The Arab kings.

and he served Sayf al-Dīn, the amīr akhūr,
and Ikhtiyār al-Dīn Ḥasan.
And from there he went out to Diyarbakr and served the sons of Shah-Arman,
and Hazārdīnārī who arose after them,
then the sons of al-ʿĀdil who ruled there;
and finally he returned to Edessa.
And when he heard that Tughril the eunuch—
who had been his friend from the time he served Ikhtiyār al-Dīn—
had become the father and counselor of the kingdom in Aleppo,
he arose and came to him.
And that undiscerning eunuch did not receive him with honor,
as was fitting for him.
And when he was blamed for this, he said:
"Because of his Christianity, I disregard him."
And that Ḥasnūn the physician remained in Aleppo, being grieved and very distressed.
And when he wished to return to Edessa, he was seized by a severe fever,
and with the fever he suffered from diarrhea and dysentery of the bowels,
and he died in Aleppo itself,
and was buried in the church of Mart Barbara in it.
For he was a venerable old man, well-built in body,
and sufficiently skilled in medicine,
and partially in philosophy.
It is said of him
that he meditated constantly on the Book of the Luqari (of the Lubari) {OCR?}.
And his conversation was very pleasant,
and he retained a multitude of stories of ancient kings and sages, and of those he had seen in his own days.
And in his time there was also renowned in Edessa the excellent physician Gabriel,
who wrote many books, both medical and philosophical, in Syriac.
And in the year 626,
were encamped {OCR?}:
they agreed to take Damascus and its territory from al-Malik al-Nāṣir Dāwūd, the son of al-Muʿaẓẓam, their brother,
and that the city of Damascus as far as the high place of Fīq should belong to al-Ashraf,
and from Fīq as far as Gaza to al-Kāmil,
and that al-Ashraf should give to al-Malik al-Nāṣir places in the East instead of Damascus.
And al-Malik al-Nāṣir agreed with them.
And when he went to Damascus to take his possessions and his household and leave,
he repented,
and was not willing to surrender [it].
And al-Ashraf took his own forces, and also some from al-Kāmil,
and went and encamped against Damascus. Tughril {OCR?}.
